# Redline

## Setup
First Create a .env file containing these variables:

```env
obs_password=""
app_key=""
app_secret=""
refresh_token=""
```

The following instructions were taken from the Dropbox site. 

**NOTE:** This tutorial assumes you have created a Dropbox app, and granted necessary permissions 

### 1. Go to this link, replace APPKEY with your app key generated by your Dropbox App
```bash
https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=APPKEYHERE&response_type=code&token_access_type=offline
```

### 2. Follow the instructions, click allow, and copy the code, this is your authorization code.

### 3. Run the following curl command in your terminal, replacing `YOUR_AUTHORIZATION_CODE` (Previous Step), `YOUR_APP_KEY`, and `YOUR_APP_SECRET` with your actual credentials:
```bash
curl https://api.dropbox.com/oauth2/token -d code=YOUR_AUTHORIZATION_CODE -d grant_type=authorization_code -u YOUR_APP_KEY:YOUR_APP_SECRET
```

### 4. Find the refresh token near the bottom, and copy it


### 5. Use the `APP_KEY`, `APP_SECRET`, `REFRESH_TOKEN`, and place it in the .env file

To get their OBS token, follow these next instructions


### 1. In OBS, Non-Safe Mode, Select Tools --> WebSocket Server Settings

![WebSocket Server Settings](Assets/image-2.png)

### 2. On This page, Select enable WebSocket Server, also go ahead and copy the server password, then hit apply and ok.

![WebSocket Server Settings Panel](Assets/image-3.png)

### 3. In an .env file that you will create, paste the password you previously copied.

```env
obs_password=""
```
